broad_diagnosis.value: Suspected metastatic malignancy involving the liver, with increased hepatic disease burden on follow-up.
broad_diagnosis.basis: Observed: multiple hypoattenuating hepatic lesions, including an ill-defined right-lobe lesion in baseline.nii.gz at native (i,j,k) approximately (185,315,430), and a much larger right-lobe mass in followup.nii.gz around (155,250,542), with additional lesions across k=526-550. Baseline liver reviewed at k=380-440 and follow-up at k=506-558. Multiplicity and marked interval increase favor malignant hepatic involvement, most likely metastases. This is an imaging inference, not histologic confirmation or a known cancer history.
alternatives: Less likely nonmalignant multifocal hepatic lesions, including infection; unenhanced CT cannot establish histology

specific_primary_diagnosis.basis: Neither NIfTI header contains a diagnosis, and the supplied CT images do not establish a primary site or histology. Hepatic lesions are nonspecific. Extensive body coverage and right-groin scar-like changes cannot identify the original tumor.
alternatives: Metastatic melanoma is compatible with extensive limb coverage and possible prior groin intervention, but neither feature is diagnostic
Other solid malignancies with hepatic metastases

age_years.basis: No age, birth date, or examination date is present in the available NIfTI headers or extensions. Skeletal maturity supports an adult appearance but cannot establish chronological age.

recorded_sex.basis: No recorded sex field or demographic record is supplied. Visible pelvic or breast anatomy does not establish recorded sex.

interval_days.basis: No acquisition dates or trustworthy elapsed-time metadata are present. These are separate three-dimensional NIfTI volumes; spatial slice spacing, affine origins, and zero timing fields do not encode the inter-examination interval. Earlier/later ordering comes only from the supplied description. Lesion growth cannot determine elapsed days.

baseline_scan_purpose.basis: baseline.nii.gz covers lower legs through the head with arms raised and no convincing intravenous enhancement; this is compatible with a CT component of a whole-body oncologic examination. Hepatic abnormalities are already visible (for example native k=430). The label baseline is relative to this pair and does not establish initial staging, pretreatment status, or the ordering indication. No requisition, PET data, or protocol description is supplied.
alternatives: Assessment before, during, or after treatment

followup_scan_purpose.basis: followup.nii.gz has extensive feet-to-head coverage and larger/more conspicuous liver lesions (native k=526-558), supporting possible oncologic reassessment. Observed worsening cannot identify why this examination was ordered or whether it was intended to assess treatment response. No clinical indication or PET series is supplied.
alternatives: Evaluation of suspected progression or new symptoms

systemic_treatment_context.basis: No medication history, treatment dates, or treatment metadata are supplied. Increased hepatic lesion burden between baseline.nii.gz (k=410-440) and followup.nii.gz (k=526-558) cannot establish whether systemic therapy occurred, its regimen, line, intent, or effectiveness. Calling this progression on chemotherapy or immunotherapy would add unsupported history.
alternatives: Imaging during or after systemic therapy, with regimen and response context unknown

surgical_context.value: Probable prior right inguinal/local intervention; procedure, indication, and timing are unestablished.
surgical_context.basis: Observed: asymmetric right inguinal skin retraction/tethering and linear soft-tissue stranding near the femoral region, present already in baseline.nii.gz (native i=160-215, j=180-225, k=220-250; representative k=230) and persisting in followup.nii.gz (i=160-210, j=155-205, k=378-410; representative k=390). Associated right-thigh subcutaneous stranding/asymmetry is visible at baseline k=160-200 and follow-up k=330-370. This favors a scar from prior local intervention but is not an operative record. No particular cancer resection or lymph-node dissection, and no operation between these scans, can be established.
alternatives: Prior inguinal node biopsy or dissection
Other prior local surgery or intervention
Nonsurgical scarring, inflammation, or lymphatic obstruction

scientific_interpretation: Broad malignancy inference is compatible with source; melanoma appears as an alternative. Exact metadata unknowns are not failures. Suggested surgery and exact acquisition context cannot be adjudicated from retained source records. Schema validity is not clinical accuracy.

audit.limits: Observed requests supplement enforced isolation; absence of source strings alone does not prove absence of source assistance. No estimate of clinical validity or unseen prior training.
